title: Shift compatibility of the actual coefficient/direct-image mate
statement:
For every scheme morphism q, normalized scalar models on its endpoints [def-sp-finite-free-direct-image-data], and compatible coefficient map a, the specified canonical comparison commutes with integer shifts. No finite-free hypothesis is needed for shift compatibility.

theorem finiteFreeDirectImageShift {Z W : Scheme.{u}} {q : Z ⟶ W}
    (sW : ScalarModel W) (sZ : ScalarModel Z)
    {R S : Coefficients q} (a : CoefficientMap R S) :
    NatTrans.CommShift (comparison sW sZ a) ℤ

source.place: Tags 07A6, 0DVC and 0D6D; shifts of the canonical restriction comparison and its conjugates.

proof.text: Use lem-sp-canonical-right-derived-adjunction-shift for the two canonical geometric derived adjunctions. The restriction/pullback isomorphism is a composite of exact-functor derived comparisons and therefore shift-compatible. In the scalar-restriction adjunct identity, take the map to be the geometric counit. The right triangle identity identifies the canonical restriction/direct-image map with the mate of the restriction/pullback inverse; hence it commutes with shifts.

Scalar adjunctions commute with the left shifts induced from restriction. Composite adjunctions do too. Expand the inverse conjugate defining balancing: it is a composite of whiskered units, the inverse restriction comparison, counits, associators and unitors. Every factor commutes with shifts. Take its mate under the geometric adjunctions; NatTrans.CommShift.mateEquiv proves shift compatibility of comparison.
